changes.why: CHK-003 counted a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 as an alert cause only once it was accepted (A handshake). The spec does not say that. INT-INTG-002 says that a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 has a command integrity error, which is a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault that triggers fatal_fault. In TL-UL, a request exists as soon as a_valid=1. INT-TL-003 says a presented request stays stable until accepted. D-017 gives only an upper bound (16 cycles), measured from acceptance; it does not forbid an earlier alert. So the checker now records cause (a) in any cycle with i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1, both in the sticky intg_seen_q and in the same-cycle term. This makes the checker follow the spec without weakening anything the spec requires. Traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 (INT-INTG-001) still never counts as a cause. Cause (b), CHK-001/002, the assertion, its counters and the CHK-003 reference are unchanged.

notes:
I changed one file, verif/sva/nnc_chk_alert.sv, to fix fault 1. I did not run any simulation or formal tool, so it is not yet confirmed that this removes the CHK-003 counterexample.

Changes:
1. Line 72 now reads `if (i_a_valid && i_a_intg_flip) intg_seen_q <= 1'b1;`.
2. Line 82 now reads `cause_a = intg_seen_q || (i_a_valid && i_a_intg_flip);`.
Both are marked with the required fix comment.

Contract wording: the contract text for CHK-003 (contract.json:366) still says "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1". It should read "a cycle with i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1". contract.json is outside the files this task lets me change, so the contract owner needs to make that edit.

CHK-004/006/007/013: these turn off from an accepted request with i_a_intg_flip=1. That matches D-017 ("After a request with i_a_intg_flip = 1 is accepted") and contract.json:1412. Making them turn off earlier would remove checking and is not part of the listed fault, so I left them as they are.

The cocotb tests have no CHK-003 check of their own. I added no assumptions and did not edit nnc_env.sv.
